_comment: Canned agent outputs for demo mode. These stand in for LLM output so the demo runs deterministically with zero credentials. Every object validates against the schemas in app/schemas.py. Set DEMO_MODE=false with an Anthropic key to run the real agents instead.

steps.subject: Quick question about Auralane HQ
steps.body: Hi Sarah, congrats on the Series A. Saw you are bringing on three AEs this quarter. Most teams at that stage hit the same wall: reps spend their first hour a day on account research instead of conversations. We build agent systems that do the research, scoring and drafting, and your reps approve everything from Slack. Worth a look?

steps.subject: How teams like yours ramp AEs faster
steps.body: Hi Sarah, following up with one concrete number: teams running agent-assisted research cut ramp time for new AEs because every call starts with a prepared brief. Happy to show you what that looks like on your own pipeline.

steps.subject: Worth a 15 minute chat?
steps.body: Hi Sarah, last note from me. If pipeline prep is not a problem worth solving this quarter, no stress. If it is, 15 minutes is enough to show you the system working end to end.

draft.personalization_notes: Anchored on the Series A and the AE hiring push. Kept the CTA soft on the final step.

steps.subject: Your first SDR hire
steps.body: Hi Marcus, saw Stackmere is hiring its first SDR alongside the enterprise launch. Before that hire starts, it is worth deciding what the machine does and what the human does. We build the machine part: research, scoring, drafts, all approved by a human in Slack. Keen to see it?

steps.body: Hi Marcus, quick follow-up. A first SDR with an agent crew behind them starts with prepared briefs and drafted sequences instead of a blank CRM. That is the difference between ramping in weeks and ramping in months.

steps.subject: Closing the loop
steps.body: Hi Marcus, last one from me. If outbound infrastructure is on your list for this quarter, 15 minutes gets you a working demo on real data. If not, good luck with the enterprise push.

steps.subject: RevOps Manager posting
steps.body: Hi Emily, noticed the RevOps Manager posting. Some of that role is judgment, and some of it is plumbing: enrichment, routing, dedupe, follow-up. We build agent systems that take the plumbing so the hire you make does the judgment work. Worth comparing notes?

steps.subject: Event follow-up that does not leak
steps.body: Hi Emily, one specific example: conference leads that get researched, scored and drafted for follow-up within the hour, with a human approving every send. That is usually the fastest win for teams with your stack.

steps.body: Hi Emily, closing the loop. If RevOps capacity is the bottleneck this quarter, I can show you a working system in 15 minutes. Either way, good luck with the hire.
